findings.issue: getPokemonPageData fetches every move detail and version group and returns move tables for all games, while the page renders only the selected game — heavy upstream fan-out on first load and a large JSON payload per Pokémon page.
findings.suggestion: Accept a game query parameter on /api/pokemon/[name] (page already has it in the URL) and build move rows only for that game, or lazily expose per-game data.

findings.issue: Every page uses useFetch<any>, discarding the types the server layer already exports; DTOs are untyped on the client so renames and shape changes won't be caught.
findings.suggestion: Move the DTO types into shared/types/ (Nuxt 4's documented location for cross-context types) or a shared module, and drop the <any> so useFetch infers them.

findings.issue: A non-OK upstream response throws, useFetch leaves data null, and the page renders 'Not found' with HTTP 200 — an upstream outage is indistinguishable from a missing resource.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish error from 404 (e.g. throw createError with statusCode 502/404 from the handler, or return {error:true}) and render an error state, ideally via error.vue.

findings.issue: On param-only navigation the component is reused and watch:[name] refetches while the old Pokémon's data (and title) stays rendered until resolve — a brief stale-content flash.
findings.suggestion: Treat pending state explicitly (use status from useFetch and gate the template), or key the page on the route param.

findings.issue: The promise cache is keyed by request-derived URLs with no bound and caches 404 nulls forever, so arbitrary distinct names accumulate entries.
findings.suggestion: Cap the cache (LRU) or only cache successful responses, leaving 404s uncached.

findings.issue: The project uses the legacy Nuxt 3 directory layout (top-level pages/, app.vue) that Nuxt 4 silently falls back to, rather than the current app/ srcDir structure the v4 docs recommend.
findings.suggestion: Move app code into app/ subdirectory (app/app.vue, app/pages/…) to match Nuxt 4's documented structure.

findings.issue: The /types page fetches the full 1025-species pokédex index and embeds it in the SSR payload to render 18 type links.
findings.suggestion: Serve a slim /api/types endpoint (or at minimum a separate useFetch key) so /types doesn't ship the whole index.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled query-string serializer (searchString/pageUrl) duplicates router.resolve/withQuery, and the 4 detail pages duplicate the same useHead title logic (e.g. app/pages/moves/[name].vue:57).
findings.suggestion: Use withQuery/router.resolve for pagination links and a tiny composable for the '… – Pokédex' title.

findings.issue: Dead definePageMeta({}) call; watch:[name] on the detail pages is redundant since useFetch already watches the reactive URL getter.
findings.suggestion: Remove the empty definePageMeta and the redundant watch options.

findings.issue: decodeURIComponent applied to getRouterParam, which already returns decoded params — double-decoding (harmless for current data names but fragile).
findings.suggestion: Drop the decodeURIComponent; use getRouterParam(event, 'name', { decode: true }) explicitly if decoding is intended.

summary: A solid, clearly-idiomatic Nuxt app: correct routing/data-fetch primitives, clean small components, careful URL-driven state and accessibility, and spec-compliant details throughout. The main merge blockers are efficiency and typing, not craft: the Pokémon endpoint eagerly builds and ships every game's move tables, and everything client-side is any-typed despite well-defined server DTOs. I'd approve after one round addressing payload weight, shared types, and the error-vs-404 conflation.
